A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AUTALIC study. All pages, tables, figures, and references support comparison; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-disagreement analyses and evaluations of logistic regression, BERT, and six LLMs in Sections 3.2.5 and 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the study's original annotation analyses and model-evaluation results, including Tables 5-7 and the agreement heatmap.

M1.justification: The contextual annotation and majority-label procedures, BERT classifier, and LLM prompting remain unchanged. The redesigned context illustration introduces no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,400 English Reddit sentences from 192 subreddits for anti-autistic ableism classification. The opening illustration reuses an existing example and does not establish an additional evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Tables 5-7 retain logistic regression, BERT, GPT-4o, Llama-3-8B, Aya-23-8B, Gemma-2-2B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-3-Mini. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 80/20 LR/BERT splits, BERT test-set-based hyperparameter selection, downsampling and n-gram settings, and three contextual LLM prompts are unchanged. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The disagreement, completion-time, prompt-variation, and safety-check analyses are retained. The redrawn context and disagreement examples contain the same cases, without additional ablation or robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same alignment mean/SD and completion-time correlation significance reporting, including R = -0.644 and p = 0.0096. Run/seed disclosure and uncertainty-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: The year-by-year publication distribution in v1 Figure 1 is removed; v2 Section 3.1.3 instead summarizes that nearly a quarter of posts were published in 2023. Tables 1-7 and the agreement heatmap retain their values, including F1 scores of 0.20 for LR, 0.04 for BERT, and 0.36 for GPT-4o.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations. No formal definition or mathematical reasoning is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: AUTALIC is the first contextual anti-autistic ableism benchmark, and existing classifiers and LLMs struggle with detection and human alignment.

C2.justification: The new opening caption restates the context and vaccine-stigma interpretation already present in Section 3.2.4. Interpretations concerning disagreement, censorship, and model size, along with the Western-perspective, Reddit, and keyword-selection limitations, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Collection and annotation instructions, text filtering, model specifications, prompts, and default-setting disclosures remain unchanged. The glossary link, stated data-release arrangements, and noncommercial-use restriction are also retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Davidson (2017) and Mann (2019) in Figure 1's caption to support its vaccine-autism and stigma discussion. The related-work section and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 3.1.3 rewrites the publication-year summary, the context-example caption is expanded, and other captions and cross-references receive limited edits. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The three sentence-example graphics are redesigned as social-media-style cards. The former context example becomes a two-panel, full-width opening Figure 1 in v2; the publication-year chart is removed, and figures and tables are repositioned throughout. This substantially revises the visual presentation while retaining the example content and table structures.

improvement.justification: v2's opening sentence-alone/context comparison communicates the dataset's central motivation more clearly than v1's context-only illustration, with an expanded caption and supporting citations. Removing the publication-year chart sacrifices some descriptive detail, but the clearer explanation provides a modest overall benefit. The experimental evidence and methodological limitations remain unchanged.
